about: The block-by-block workshop's second round of crit, from the walk-in to deep dive 1's statement (m001 to m033), as Noah left it on October 20, 2026, before the boards were cleared for round three. His notes are also in design/history/data/compass.js, word for word. Moment IDs are this round's; labels say which moment each was.

labels.m007: The splash: two cards come together
labels.m017: Who is Palit for: the statement
labels.m031: Sharing, and the palette beside the work
labels.m032: How we worked: every decision, day by day

notes.m001: lets add a heyclicky styled, subtle color grading that makes our footage feel fresh and friendly - warmer. I also want a slight film look, similar to heyclicky's videos. I also want a subtle fisheye lens just to the walk-in, it'll really add to the atmosphere. Make Cooper Union a little bigger, and rethink the specific moment of the clip you chose for us going up the stairs. Apply this to our interview/outro footage as well.
notes.m002: we shouldn't see the moment we stand before we sit, when this clip plays, we should already be on the way down, making it a quick transition from the walk-in. Refer to the walk-in notes for the coloring and effects.
notes.m007: Still not liking our splash - I want it to be snappier, and a little more creative with how the word appears? Just more profesional and fluid - check out how other big companies do a splash. The concept of the squares coming together is nice though - the colors could turn black as the word comes out
notes.m009: lets instead of the droplet, adopt the cursor quickly dragging a box around the highlighted word - feels more on-theme and professional. can we have a subtle fade with the slide up? Both in and out, making it feel more fluid and pro
notes.m010:
nice, lets make the dragged box a little bit bigger to cover the entire "storytelling". area. Also, period should come after the quotation marks.

Again, for the text that slides, lets add a subtle fade that makes it feel more pro and fluid.
notes.m011: Can we instead, drop the brief, then raise the cards, left then right? They should float/recoil into place, elegantly. I'm not sure what the colors on each card do for this section - lets make sure they actually do something meaningful, without taking too much of the focus
notes.m014: This is a great moment, but I'm a little unsure of what this means. What does it mean that the two lead back to the work? Can we simplify the language, and make sure the messaging values authenticity and ties directly to our goal?
notes.m016: The cards look good, can we name the specimen cards "Specimen card 1" and "Specimen card 2"? Also, when the palit line pushes Pantone up, pantone goes a little far. It should be closer to palit. This line can also be bigger, and be centred.
notes.m018:
not loving how the colored words shrink then go into where the boxes are - can we just drop/fade them and have them re-appear as the boxes? Will be cleaner.

All these instances of components either just fading in, or having a slide in is not what I want - I want a consistent way they appear with a mix of both, being elegant and pro looking.

Loving how it times with the scrip - we may have to slightly tune the timing with the audio recordings.
notes.m020: refer to initial overlay notes, and the appearance notes - fade in/slide in, both with elegance
notes.m022: The zoom out is so janky. Lets make it smooth, and not too sudden. Buffer it just slightly, you know? I also don't know why we're working with a screenshot of the prior version - redo the demo recording if needed, to make it as crisp and clean as possible with these changes.
notes.m023:
This looks great, I think the keybinds could fade out a little smoother, in the order you click them in. They should bump slightly also in the order you use them in, not too harshly though.

Looks great though. Lets keep this as we rebuild this demo section
notes.m024:
Good beats and timing, but the initial bump for the color coming into the side chip feels a little off? Can we make it more elegant, with a smoother animation? Feel free to take slightly more time animating the bumps.

Also, just in general for this section, the desktop is like a square. Can it be rounded a little, and be windowed by the white background slightly? Just so it looks equal when we zoom out of the window.
notes.m025: great, just refer to prior notes about movement, keybinds, bumps, and whatnot
notes.m026: The demo doesn't act like the app - the blocks should be reactive whenever you hover over them, even slightly, which should be reflected. Make it subtle, but true to how our app works now. The transition to opening the today page looks pretty good, but I feel as though the animation could be just a little bit more fancy and slower
notes.m027: So good, just refer to prior notes about keybind bumps and the slowing down/decorating of the appear animations - just slightly to make it feel more elevated and timed
notes.m028:
specturm scroll still doesn't feel very human scroll like, lets make it more smooth, but authentic. The zoom for naming is awesome.

The appear animation could again, be slightly more elevated, slowed, and decorated/timed.

Refer to prior notes about keybind bumps too.
notes.m029: I think the color card could slightly slide up when it fades in, just to give it a more elevated look. Loving the zoom for the scratchpad, looks good. Can we make it reflect human typing just a little more? Maybe even a semi-typo, a quick delete, then correction? I'm talking maybe 2 or 3 letters.
notes.m030: looks good, lets just be mindful of smoothing the camera movement and zooms, which goes for all sections of this video - lets be smooth/elegant when we can, especially when we need quick pans and movements.
notes.m031: Not sure what the animation is in the background when we close the palette window, something weird happens with the colors when you go to close the palette window. Good camera zooms that make the feature feel coherent we could even zoom in slightly more, before zooming out.
notes.m032: we should load the blocks a little quicker, but have slight pauses between loading the different days. The counting up too for the stats, lets have them a little quicker, timing them alongside the blocks we load on the days. Lets also be mindful of the placement of the section - the header, blocks, stats, and legend at the bottom - they should be coherent and legible
